title: First Tor vanishes for the second syzygy over two variables
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x_0,x_1], and let k as an S-module mean restriction of scalars along constant coefficient. Use Tor as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let F_0 and F_1 be S-modules in the ring universe with specified finite bases, q_0:F_0 to M a surjective S-linear map, and q_1:F_1 to ker(q_0) a surjective S-linear map. M may have a different universe. Then Tor_1^S(ker(q_1),k) has subsingleton carrier. No grading assumptions are required.

proof.text: Use the small quotient F₀/ker(q₀), canonically isomorphic to M by surjectivity. Its quotient map has exactly ker(q₀) as kernel. Transport q₁ along that kernel equality; its kernel is unchanged up to the induced linear equivalence. The finite bases make F₀ and F₁ free. Apply [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shifting] to the two short exact kernel sequences to identify Tor₁(ker(q₁),k) with Tor₃(F₀/ker(q₀),k). This stays in the ring universe regardless of the universe of M.

proof.text: In the proved private helper third_tor_constantCoeff, form the S-linear constant-coefficient map c:S→k with the restricted scalar action; it is surjective since c(C(a))=a. Use [lem-sc-p1-koszul-resolution] and identify ker(c) with ker(q): the ideal spanned by X₀,X₁ is idealOfVars, whose first-power support criterion says exactly that the coefficient at zero vanishes. Restrict the Koszul map g:S²→S to g′:S²→ker(c); exactness of g,q proves its surjectivity. Exactness and injectivity of f give a short exact sequence 0→S→S²→ker(c)→0. Apply [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shifting] to this sequence and 0→ker(c)→S→k→0. Its isomorphism identifies Tor₃(k,N) with Tor₁(S,N), which is zero by Mathlib isZero_Tor'_succ_of_projective because S is free and projective. Thus no bounded-resolution packaging is needed.

theorem second_syzygy_tor_vanishes {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M]
    (F₀ F₁ : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k))
    (r₀ r₁ : ℕ)
    (b₀ : Module.Basis (Fin r₀) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) F₀)
    (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) F₁)
    (q₀ : F₀ →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] M) (hq₀ : Function.Surjective q₀)
    (q₁ : F₁ →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] q₀.ker) (hq₁ : Function.Surjective q₁) :
    Subsingleton (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) 1).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) q₁.ker)).obj
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        (MvPolynomial.constantCoeff : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k →+* k)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of k k)))
